audit.report: A replayable inventory batch (pid 112488) held an open transaction for 4.0 seconds and blocked 12 checkout sessions, degrading checkout to 27% success over 30 seconds versus the 95% SLO. About $13,382 per minute of revenue was at risk, exceeding the business's 60-second tolerance for degradation. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the batch; the Continuity Guardian requested revision because change-calendar evidence was missing, then accepted once the registry confirmed no active change-calendar window covered the workload. The batch was terminated in round 2, locks were released, and verification showed 36/36 checkouts succeeded over 10 seconds at 100% with no protected settlements aborted. The business is recovered.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory workload (pid 112488) was idle in transaction and held locks that 12 checkout sessions waited on, causing checkout timeouts and SLO breach.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, check workload registry and change-calendar evidence together before terminating so the Continuity Guardian cannot request a revision and cost a round.
Capture change-calendar coverage for inventory_reconcile in advance so termination decisions on batch_replayable_inventory are not blocked by missing I2 evidence during an incident.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian did not waste a round; its first proposal was sound but lacked change-calendar evidence required by invariant I2. The Continuity Guardian correctly invoked I2/I3, requested the missing evidence, and accepted once the registry probe confirmed no active change-calendar window.
follow_ups: Add change-calendar coverage for inventory_reconcile (batch_replayable_inventory) so future terminations are pre-approved or owner-consulted without a missing-evidence revision.
Review why pid 112488 was idle in transaction for 4.0 seconds and whether batch_replayable_inventory should hold checkout-blocking locks during peak traffic.
